title: UPSC CSE - Medieval India - Provincial Kingdoms in Medieval India
subject: Medieval India

questions.q: Who of the following rulers of medieval India gave permission to the Portuguese to build a fort at Bhatkal?
questions.explain: Emperor Krishnadevaraya allowed the Portuguese to build a fort in Bhatkal in 1510.
questions.subject: Medieval India

questions.q: In medieval India, the term Fanam referred to:
questions.explain: During the Vijaynagar Empire, Fanams were coins used in day-to-day life. Fanam was usually a small fraction of the main currency (Pagoda or Varaha). The Travancore Fanam was a form of money issued by the State of Travancore in South India, which is today mostly a part of Kerala. Fanams and Chuckrams were renowned to be among the world's tiniest coins.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs :
King Dynasty
1. Nannuka Chandela
2. Jayashakti Paramara
3. Nagabhata II Gurjara-Pratihara
4. Bhoja Rashtrakuta

How many pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain:
Pair 1 is correct: Nanuka was the founder of the Chandela Dynasty.
Pair 2 is incorrect: Jayashakti was also a Chandela Ruler.
Pair 3 is correct: Nagabhata II belonged to the Gurjara Pratihara Dynasty.
Pair 4 is incorrect: Bhoja was a Parmara.

questions.q:
With reference to Indian history, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. The Nizamat of Arcot emerged out of Hyderabad state.
2. The Mysore kingdom emerged out of Vijayanagara Empire.
3. Rohilkhand kingdom was formed out of the territories occupied by Ahmad Shah Durrani.
questions.explain: Statement 1 is not correct: Nizamat of Arcot was established by Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb and was the legal dependency of the Nizam of Hyderabad; it did not emerge from the Hyderabad state.\nStatement 2 is correct: Mysore was transformed from a viceroyalty of the Vijayanagara Empire into an autonomous state by the Wodeyar dynasty.\nStatement 3 is not correct: The states of Rohilkhand and the kingdom of the Bangash Pathans were a fallout of the Afghan migration into India. Ali Muhammad Khan took advantage of the collapse of authority in North India following Nadir Shah's invasion to set up a petty kingdom, Rohilkhand.

questions.q: Which one of the following foreign travellers elaborately discussed diamonds and diamond mines of India?
questions.explain: Jean-Baptiste Tavernier (1605‒89) was one of the most renowned travellers of 17th-century Europe. He was a jewel merchant who between 1632 and 1668 made six voyages to the East. While on his travels to India he discovered and discussed diamonds and diamond mines of India extensively.

questions.q: Which one of the following was a very important seaport in the Kakatiya kingdom?
questions.explain: Motupalli was an important seaport in the kingdom of Ganpati (an important Kakatiya ruler), frequented by foreign merchants. Italian traveler Marco Polo who had visited the port in 1287 AD, had given a vivid account on the flourishing trade activities at the port during the reign of Kakatiya queen Rudrama Devi.

questions.q:
Regarding the taxation systems of Krishna Deva, the ruler of Vijayanagar, consider the following statements:
1. The tax rate of land was fixed depending on the quality of the land.
2. Private owners of workshops paid an industry tax.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is correct: In the reign of Krishna Deva, the entire land was classified into four parts: the wetland, the dry land, the orchards, and the woods and the tax rate of land was fixed depending on the quality of the land.\nStatement 2 is correct: Besides land tax, the government also levied other taxes. Private owners of workshops paid an industry tax.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Medieval Indian State Present Region
1. Champaka Central India
2. Durgara Jammu
3. Kuluta Malabar

Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
questions.explain: The foothills of the Himalayas lent themselves quite well to such small kingdoms, owing to the nature of the country. The ninth century saw the rise of several hill states, some of which maintained their identity until recent years. States such as Champaka (Chamba in Himachal Pradesh), Durgara (Jammu), Trigarta (Jalandhar), Kuluta (Kulu in Himachal Pradesh), Kumaon and Garhwal managed to remain outside the main areas of conflict in the northern plains.

questions.q: Who of the following founded a new city on the south bank of a tributary to river Krishna and undertook to rule his new kingdom as the agent of a deity to whom all the land south of the river Krishna was supposed to belong?
questions.explain: Vijayanagara or city of victory, was the name of both a city and an empire. Harihara I and Bukka founded the Vijayanagar Empire in the fourteenth century. It stretched from the river Krishna in the north to the extreme south of the Peninsula (Krishna-Tungabhadra doab). Harihara I established control over the valley of the Tungabhadra River (a tributary of Krishna).

questions.q: In medieval India, the designations 'Mahattara' and 'Pattakila' were used for
questions.explain: Mahattara means the principal, chief, or oldest person, the most respectable person. In Medieval India Mahattara was Headman among the Agrahdrinas, that is, the owner of an agrahara, a rent-free village in the possession of Brahmanas. Pattakila means village headman, the same as modern-day Patel or Patil. Pattakila is believed to be the king's representative in the village.
